promptHead: Athlete goal: 5K (Corrowmore Harvest 5K) on Sun Nov 15 2026, 3 weeks out, target run the whole way.

new.headline: Two weeks away from running does not reset you, so we step back in gently this week with three short walk-runs and then see where you are. Finishing the 5K on Sun Nov 15 is the priority now, even if some of it is walked.

flags.title: Two weeks off
flags.detail: Mum came first, and that was right. We rebuild carefully now, not chase lost sessions.

flags.title: Sleep and stress
flags.detail: 6 hours and high stress make hard running feel harder. Keep efforts conversational this week.

flags.title: Race is closer than it reads
flags.detail: Sun Nov 15 is 4 weekends away, not 4 full weeks. Plan around that, not a bigger gap.

flags.title: Goal check
flags.detail: running the whole 5K was the dream, finishing it is the win. We may need a run-walk race plan.

answers.question: I haven't run for two weeks. Do I have to start again from the beginning? And is the 5K in four weeks still realistic?
answers.answer:
No, you do not start from the beginning. Two weeks off at this stage softens your fitness a little but does not erase it, and the walk-run sessions you did in September are still in your legs. We drop back one small step this week, not all the way to day one, and build again from there.

On the race: it is 3 weeks and 6 days away, not 4, so time is tighter than it feels. Finishing the Corrowmore Harvest 5K is realistic and I want you on that start line. Running every single step without a walk break is less certain given the gap, so I would like us to keep that as the dream and have a run-walk plan as plan B. We will decide which to aim for after next weekend's longer session.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

You missed all three planned walk-runs in the week of Oct 12 – 18, which was the right call with your mum in hospital, so there is nothing to make up and no blame to carry. The job now is to get you running again without making your legs sore from one big session.

I have kept your usual Mon, Wed, Sat pattern and dropped the first session back to 6 rounds of 2 minutes running and 1 minute walking, which is a notch below where you were in late September. Wednesday steps up to 7 rounds and Saturday to 8 rounds, so by the weekend you are back on the longest session you had done before the break. That is a gentle climb, not a jump.

Keep every run conversational, which for you has been around 7:40/km on the run portions, and do not push the pace to catch up. If a session feels hard, shorten the last round rather than skip the next day. Your sleep is thin and stress is high, so easy really means easy this week.

Next week I want to add one slightly longer Saturday session and one short piece at race effort, so we have one proper look at race pace before Nov 15. For now, just get three steady sessions in the bank and come back to me honestly about how they felt.

settingsProposalBullets: Add a race plan B to your goal: finish the Corrowmore Harvest 5K with run-walk intervals if running the whole way is not on by race week.
Note that family caregiving is an ongoing stressor through at least October, so planned sessions may need to flex.

safetyCallouts.title: Low sleep and high stress.
safetyCallouts.body: Six hours and ongoing family stress raise how hard any run feels and slow recovery. If you feel unwell, dizzy or unusually breathless on a run, stop and walk home, and speak to your GP before pushing on.
